messages:
oncall-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT PAGE: p99 streaming latency spike detected in us-west-2 (models/redwood-llama-13b). Auto-page to oncall. root_metrics: p95=420ms p99=14.8s; streaming stalls observed.

maya: I'm on it. seeing alerts from metrics pipeline — p99 jump ~14:05 UTC, sustained. link: https://console/redwood/metrics/streaming/us-west-2 (posted)

ton y: @maya can you confirm customer impact? which tenants routed to these nodes?

maya: BrightSim-prod and some internal canaries. BrightSim experiencing request timeouts/retries -> support already seeing 3x error rate.

jess: paging logs show a cluster of correctable ECC errors on GPU node gpu-node-17 starting ~14:03. dmesg snippet below.

jess: ```
[Wed Mar 10 14:03:12] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=4821, GPU 2: 30 ECC errors corrected
[Wed Mar 10 14:03:13] nvidia: ecc: correctable 1, uncorrectable 0
[Wed Mar 10 14:04:01] thermal: GPU 2 temp rise to 92C, throttle engaged
```

samir: nvtop / nvidia-smi shows GPU 2 running at 100% memory, 98% util during these requests. temps climbing to mid-90s and driver logs show ECC correctables.

infra-bot: Automatic mitigation suggestion: mark node gpu-node-17 UNHEALTHY, redirect new streams, drain existing sessions with 30s grace. To execute: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

maya: I initiated drain + removed node from LB pool at 14:09 UTC. Traffic shifted to fallback pool (smaller quantizada models) at 14:10.

tony: Good. Any immediate improvement in latency after traffic shift?

jess: Partial improvement for new requests: p99 dropped from 14.8s -> ~1.2s for fallback routes. Streaming tail for in-flight sessions still seeing stalls until KV cache sanity completes.

maya: Customer update: raised SES to BrightSim at 14:12, telling them we're mitigating and reviewing root cause. CS noted some long-lived streaming sessions were retried causing duplicates.

ops-tilly: @samir can you paste `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,THERMAL` output for gpu-node-17?

samir: ```
==============NVSMI LOG==============
GPU 2
    Product Name                    : NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB
    ECC Errors (Corrected)          : 124 (since boot)
    ECC Errors (Uncorrected)        : 0
    Temperature                      : 94 C
    Power Draw                       : 395 W
    GPU Utilization                  : 98 %
```

jess: Looks like correctable ECC errors spiking correlated with thermal. Could be hardware degradation on that card or bad airflow on chassis.

maya: We've flagged the node for replacement and opened a ticket with colo ops. But we need to confirm if this pattern is transient (flare) or progressive.

tony: What about automatic fallback policy? Did anything misroute because of stale model-variant compatibility?

maya: Fallback worked as intended — route policy sent new requests to `redwood-llama-13b-quant8` variant. However sessions that had established large KV caches on the affected node experienced stall while we drained; streaming worker didn't checkpoint fast enough.

ops-tilly: For live mitigation: 1) take node out of rotation (done), 2) increase streaming-worker checkpoint frequency to reduce long tail for clients, 3) temporarily relax SLO alerts to avoid noise while we triage. Any objections?

samir: Agree on checkpoint freq increase — I'll push a quick config bump: `STREAMING_CHECKPOINT_MS=500` -> previously 2000. Rolling update to streaming workers in us-west-2 now.

infra-bot: Deploy started: rollout/streaming-workers-us-west-2 v2.14 -> v2.14+checkpoint. Will monitor.

jess: Also adding short-term kernel parameter to reduce ECC correction retries? Not sure. Need hardware team input before fiddling with ECC policy.

maya: High-level customer impact: BrightSim saw ~7% of requests error out or retry during 14:03-14:12 window. We classify as P1 impact (SLO breach for p99 streaming latency).

tony: Agree classify P1. Escalating to eng-sre and engage hardware on-call for node investigation. @samir please coordinate with hardware.

samir: Reached out to colo ops (ticket #COLO-9876). Requested immediate swap of GPU card and run burn-in. ETA on tech is 2-3 hours.

maya: For incident comms — I'll draft a status page update: summary, mitigation done (traffic shifted, node drained), customer impact, next steps (node replacement, postmortem).

ops-tilly: Any sign of other nodes with similar ECC spikes? Run a quick cluster scan?

jess: Running query across nodes for ECC correctable > 50 in last 24h. Current noisy nodes: gpu-node-03 (60), gpu-node-17 (124), gpu-node-42 (58). Not widespread but suspicious cluster of older chassis.

samir: Marking nodes 03 and 42 for scheduled review — not immediate drain unless they spike further. Also scheduling overnight stress test on those nodes to catch intermittent flake.

maya: Questions for postmortem: - why did ECC correctables lead to thermal throttle vs graceful degradation? - why did in-flight sessions stall during drain and TTL of KV cache wasn't sufficient? - do we need better preemptive rotation for nodes with rising correctables?

tony: Also add: verify node telemetry alerting about ECC rate thresholds (correctable per minute/5m) so we auto-evacuate earlier.

infra-bot: Suggested post-incident runbook changes: add ECC rate metric to node health, auto-cordon threshold = 100 correctables / 5m, and reduce drain grace to prefer new request routing.

maya: Putting owner tags: incident lead = maya, infra lead = samir, runtime follow-up = jess. I'll schedule a 60-min postmortem tomorrow 09:00 PST.

jess: Final status: mitigated at 14:12 UTC (traffic shifted + node drained). Continued monitoring for 2 hours.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: resolved->mitigated at 14:12 UTC. SLO alert muted for 2h. Please follow-up with postmortem notes.

maya: Thanks everyone. I'll post updates to #status-page once postmortem time is set.

(reacts: maya :thumbsup:, tony :eyes:)
